name: Dot drop flood
looks: A field of dots in perspective sits on a dark ground. One accent dot falls under real gravity with a readout of its speed, hits on the downbeat, squashes hard and sends a ring shockwave through the floor, then stretches into a line that carries a travelling wave before thickening into a band that floods the whole frame on the next downbeat.
build: Draw the floor dots and the shockwave ring on one 2D canvas from the master clock, with the fall following true projectile physics (y = y0 + v0t + gt^2/2) until impact and a damped spring for the squash. Grow the flood band's height to the full frame on a power3-in ease, timed to the beat.
sound: A sub thump on impact, a soft tick per readout update, a riser under the wave, and a hit on the flood.
prompt: Open on a field of dots in perspective; drop one accent dot into it under real gravity so it falls, hits hard on a downbeat, squashes and sends a ring shockwave outward, then stretches into a travelling line that thickens into a band flooding the whole frame on the next downbeat. Use the falling dot as a mark that can recur through the film, changing meaning at each return.
source: the 2026 Opus showreels (reference studied 2026-10-06); built in examples/reel-2026-10-06.html, S1.
